assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct observation in 2012 of the long-predicted scalar boson completes the experimental verification of electroweak symmetry breaking in the Standard Model. The discovery is at the centre: a concrete, unambiguous new particle, with decades of detector conception and construction behind it and a lasting programme of coupling measurements.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experimental side was left open. Credit is real but diffuse across two collaborations of thousands. The three proposed names are the founding proposers/leaders of ATLAS and CMS (two ATLAS, one CMS); Gianotti was spokesperson at the time of the announcement and is an equally defensible choice. Any three-person configuration is a compromise.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and by the full LHC dataset; properties are consistent with a Standard Model Higgs. Recognition is arguably overdue and mature.
uncertainties: Which individuals, rather than the collaborations, deserve the credit is genuinely contested.
I rely on memory for the roles of the named individuals and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, opened neutrino astronomy and required building a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice. A clear discovery with a new window on the Universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA; Karle and Spiering held central leadership and design roles in AMANDA/IceCube. The credited three form a plausible, if collaboration-dependent, configuration; other IceCube leaders could also be argued for.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established at high significance; source identification is more recent and still evolving (the TXS association has about 3 sigma significance, the Galactic plane result is newer). Core discovery is mature, source astrophysics less so.
uncertainties: Origin of most of the flux remains unresolved.
Allocation among long-standing project leaders is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators established a new classification of quantum matter: the Z2 invariant, the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe, and protected surface states in three dimensions. The concept is original, clear and has reshaped condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) provided the theory; Molenkamp's group gave the experimental realisation of 2D quantum spin Hall transport (following a theoretical proposal I recall from others not on this list); Hasan led the first 3D ARPES observation. Mele and also uncredited theorists complicate a fair three-person split. I choose theory plus two experimental pillars.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many independent groups over about 15 years; applications remain limited but the physical understanding is stable.
uncertainties: Theorists outside the credited list contributed decisively to the HgTe prediction.
Mele versus Hasan for the third slot is a difficult call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a highly productive and original field combining theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental observation. The credited names map cleanly onto a theory-plus-experiment prize. Other experimentalists (for example, the Dean and Young-related efforts) are not credited, so fairness is limited by the list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups; the nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, and the field is young, so the timing could be premature.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of superconductivity is unresolved.
Fast-moving field; later discoveries may rearrange credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength proposal and developed to 10^-18 precision, is a transformational precision-measurement instrument with implications for redefinition of the second and tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye's group drove the performance to the best accuracy and stability. Two names give a clean, defensible attribution; others (Hall, Hansch) have already been honoured in 2005 for related comb technology.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reach comparable performance; the redefinition of the second is pending, so full recognition could be timely but could also wait.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier frequency-comb recognition may weigh against it.
Ordering relative to other metrology candidates is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of the baryon acoustic peak in the galaxy distribution gave cosmology a calibrated standard ruler, underpinning dark-energy measurements and the precision distance scale. Clear, original and of lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS luminous red galaxies) and the 2dFGRS team (Cole, Colless) reported the peak in 2005 essentially simultaneously. Credit is shared between two surveys; the proposed trio reflects this. The theoretical prediction predates the detection and has uncredited contributors.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many surveys through BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, although current tensions in dark-energy interpretation are unresolved. The technique is mature.
uncertainties: Prior theoretical work on acoustic features is not represented in the credited names.
Cosmological prizes in 2006, 2011 and 2019 may reduce appetite for another.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging of M87* and Sgr A* provides direct visual evidence for black-hole shadows, a striking and verified confirmation of strong-field gravity, building on the 2020 recognition of black-hole theory and the Galactic centre.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT, and Narayan contributed foundational accretion-flow theory. The result is a collaboration product of hundreds, so any selection of individuals is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and polarisation results published; further tests are ongoing. Reasonably mature, but the physical constraints on gravity are still modest.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit is hard to allocate.
Scientific constraints beyond imaging remain limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created the architecture for strong coupling of superconducting qubits to resonators and underlies readout and control in current quantum processors. Conceptually clear and technologically influential.
assessment.attribution: Blais and Schoelkopf with Wallraff authored the founding theory and first strong-coupling experiments in 2004. Other superconducting-circuit pioneers were honoured in 2025, which may overlap and complicate this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and now industrial; the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may have partly consumed the committee's appetite for this area.
uncertainties: Whether this is a distinct discovery or an enabling technology.
